features.breakout: guide, System Breakout Capabilities: 1 x 800G, 2 x 400G, 4 x 200G, 2 x 200G, 8 x 100G, 1 x 400G and 4 x 100G modes; odd-numbered front ports support up to 8x breakout and even-numbered up to 2x ("due to ASIC limitation").
features.optics-osfp: OSFP 800G optics and DAC: up to 20 W / 30 W transceivers, up to 4 m DAC, ZR/ZR+ coherent modules supported; up to 16 ports of 30 W optics on ports 1, 5, 9, 13, 49, 53, 57, 61 (upper row) and 4, 8, 12, 16, 52, 56, 60, 64 (bottom row). Tested in the guide's breakout table: OSFP 2x FR4 (dual duplex LC), OSFP 2x VR4 and 2x DR4 (dual MPO-8), OSFP DR8 (MPO-16) and a 400G OSFP AOC.
features.optics-sfp28: SFP28 25G optics; the guide notes 1G transceivers are supported once speed and FEC are configured. No SFP28 module is listed in the tested table.
features.timing: IEEE 1588 1-step and 2-step time stamping; transparent and boundary clock; SyncE clock recovery (timing option)

physical.weight-note: 30 kg (datasheet and guide spec table; configuration not stated)

platform.bmc: optional BMC system management - RunBMC, OpenBMC
platform.cpu: Intel Xeon D x86, 4-core (up to 8-core), 2.9 GHz, COM Express

power.power-input: 100-240 VAC auto-ranging 47-63 Hz, or 180-300 VDC auto input

configs.description: The one ordering code the datasheet lists: 2U, 64 x 800GbE, COM Express 4-core CPU, 32 GB DDR, 128 GB SSD, front-to-back airflow. This is a fixed switch, so the base configuration is the box as it is bought - four 2000 W supplies and three fan modules in, as the rear elevation draws them, and the cages empty.
configs.name: ac-f2b

gaps.wanted: What the four lenses in each column's legend row mean and which port each serves. Neither the guide nor the datasheet has an LED section: the guide's overview callouts name the ports, the management jacks and the four system lamps and stop, and the datasheet mentions no LED at all. Two lamps per port is drawn, left pair to the upper port.
What the two lamps on each supply and the one on each fan module mean. The supplies' lamps carry tiny rotated legends that Figure 2 does not resolve; no document names them.

What the three small light squares between the STAT, ALM, PSU and FAN lamps are. A drawing or photograph of the cluster at 15 px/mm or better settles whether they are lenses and whether anything should be punched there.

Orderable part numbers for the 2000 W supply and the fan module. The datasheet's ordering table lists only the system (R4028-F9002-A1) and the guide's FRU pages give removal steps without part numbers, so both components are named for their form rather than their PN.

Orthographic drawings of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's Side View and rear three-quarter view and the two product renders show all four at an angle: a plain lid with two stamped handles and two long pressings, and side walls carrying rail screws. Each face carries an `empty:` sentence.

Which way each OSFP bank faces. Figure 1 reads as 0/0 in the upper bank and 180/180 in the lower (a stacked 2x1 cage on each face of one board), the drawing here keeps 0/180 in both, and #799 first proposed 0/0 throughout. A photograph of the front, or a decision on the elevation's reading, settles it; until then every pair is held in stack-exceptions.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port group osfp800 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

colour.note: THE FRONT PANEL IS BLACK and the body, rear and FRU frames are bright metal - Celestica's two product renders sample the front at RGB 27-33 and the rear strips at 215. The guide's CAD elevation renders the panel mid-grey (68, 73, 79) and was not used for colour. The front's black is drawn as a `faceplate` decor plate between the side lattices, because a chassis has one colour and the DS5000's is the bright one.

gate-1.note: PASSES ON BOTH FACES. Figure 1's chassis body, between the ear fold lines (the ears are drawn and are NOT modelled), spans x 152.2-2579.0 and y 107.0-590.8 px by half-maximum edge reads - 2426.8 x 483.8 px against the stated 438.5 x 87 mm, 5.534 px/mm across and 5.561 down, 0.48% apart. Figure 2 spans x 393.0-2810, y 47.5-529.5 - 5.512 and 5.540, 0.51% apart. Each axis is measured on its own scale. AND THE FACE IS ORTHOGRAPHIC, NOT MERELY THE RIGHT SHAPE: fitting the sixteen OSFP column centres on each of the four rows to x = first + (i//4)*B + (i%4)*p gives an rms of 0.021-0.052 mm, and adding a quadratic term moves the ends of the row by at most 0.14 mm - there is no perspective in it. The pitch the fit returns, 23.23, is within 0.01 mm of the 23.2353 the AIS800-64O measured independently on Edgecore's own drawing of a Tomahawk 5 OSFP wall, which is a scale check the figure did not supply.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-09-26: Celestica's product page for the DS5000 carries a "now shipping" banner and no end-of-sale notice; the datasheet is dated 2025-10-09. None announced.

power.note: The guide's spec table and the datasheet both give "Power Consumption (W) <4000W", unqualified as to measure, scope or ambient; it is filed as power-draw-max-w per the library's rule for an unqualified figure. Four 2000 W supplies in a 2+2 arrangement is 4000 W with two failed, which is the vendor's own ceiling. No per-fan figure is published anywhere; the L27 warning on the fan module stands.

sources.note: TWO SOURCES AND TWO PRODUCT RENDERS. The DS5000 hardware guide on Celestica's documentation portal (22 pages converted to markdown, 31 figures), whose "DS5000 System Overview" page carries the spec table and four figures - Figure 1 Front View (2965 x 783), Figure 2 Rear View (3121 x 663), Figure 3 Side View and an untitled rear three-quarter view - plus the FRU removal pages and the breakout table; and the DS5000 datasheet (cls_branded_datasheet_DS5000_100925, 2 pages, 2025-10-09), which repeats the spec table and adds the ordering code, the fan redundancy and the software list. Figures 1 and 2 are CAD elevations, not photographs, with callouts and red port numerals drawn over them. NO SQUARE-ON PHOTOGRAPH EXISTS in anything found. Celestica's product page (cls.celestica.com/hardware-platforms/ds5000/) carries two three-quarter renders - the front alone and front plus rear side by side - fetched and kept as intake photos; they fail any face-on check and were used for COLOUR and COUNTS only. www.celestica.com answered HTTP 429 and was not retried.

the-grounding-point.note: Figure 2's "Ground lug" callout points at a copper bracket on the left strip, x 0.4-9.5, y 42.4-71.0, under a circled earth symbol at (4.95, 38.9): a ring lug at its top and two black Phillips screws at y 57.3 and 66.6. The guide's Ground Lug Installation page says that bracket is the ground lug assembly (GLA), shipped in the accessory kit and "not applicable to the AC SKU versions". SO THE BRACKET AND LUG ARE NOT DRAWN - they are a kit part with a cable on it, the same class as a cord retainer - and the two screws that fix it and the printed earth mark are.

the-legends.note: READ AT MATCHED SCALE, AND THE FIRST READING WAS WRONG. A thresholded blob sweep first put the arrows at +/-10.2 and the numerals at +/-8.9; laid over the render at 6x (33 px/mm) the figure's own arrows sit at -9.37/-9.4 and +9.6 and the one-digit numerals' centres at -7.86/-7.6 and +7.8 - the blob sweep had merged each arrow with the gasket fingers beside it. So the arrows are at +/-9.5 and the numerals hug them from inside: the odd numeral STARTS at -8.25 and the even one ENDS at +8.25, so a two-digit numeral grows towards the lamps, as the figure's "10" and "14" do. Arrows, numerals and lamps share one centreline, y 14.85 above the upper bank and 82.55 below the lower (the lamps first read 15.10 and 82.75). Cap height about 0.9 mm, so font-size 1.3. At 5.5 px/mm a numeral is five pixels tall: positions are measured, glyph weight is not.

the-lug-tag.note: Figure 1's "Lug tag" callout is celestica/lug-tag@1, Celestica's slide-out information card, standing on end in a slot in the inner left lattice column. READ AT 14x (77.5 px/mm) THE FIRST DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG: I had called it a tag hanging on a loop. The close-up shows a black card x 11.8-14.5, y 56.4-78.8 (22.4 long) in a slot x 11.5-14.7, y 56.1-79.2 (3.2 x 23.1), the model name printed along it reading bottom to top, and the panel printing LUG TAG beside it, x 15.4-17.4, y 61.9-74.1, also bottom to top - the DS3001's arrangement. The part's 23.0 x 4.0 slot matches to 0.1 mm on the long axis. It is seated rotate 270 (lip up) centred on the slot at (13.1, 67.65), label DS5000.

the-management-cluster.note: Read on a 3x and an 8x crop of Figure 1 in chassis millimetres. A silver shell x 407.4-420.6, y 5.3-36.2 holds two RJ-45 jacks ON THEIR SIDES - contacts drawn down the left, keyway notch on the right, each 10.8 wide and 12.3-12.6 tall - centred at x 414.9, y 14.03 (CONSOLE) and 27.97 (MGMT), a 13.94 pitch against std/rj45-ganged@2's 13.97, so that cell turned 270 is what is seated. The MGMT jack takes common/rj45-ganged-eth@1, the same cell with the two keyway-corner lamps the library gives every Ethernet jack (L76); Figure 1 draws a round feature inside MGMT's face and resolves no lamps, so the lamps are the family rule and not a reading. A USB-A in its own shell x 407.4-420.6, y 39.5-44.9. RST, a small dark button at (420.2, 48.9), legended to its left. Two SFP28 cages in one shell x 401.9-417.6, y 51.5-77.0, centred 56.4 and 71.4, with a 4.5 mm band between them carrying four green triangles, legended 65 above and 66 below. Four rectangular yellow-green lenses at x 420.4, y 56.3, 63.7, 71.2 and 78.65 (a 7.45 pitch), about 1.3 x 2.7, legended STAT, ALM, PSU and FAN on their sides to the right. CONSOLE, MGMT and SS are printed on their sides to the left of their ports.

the-numbering-runs-down-each-column.note: READ OFF THE FIGURE, NOT INFERRED. Figure 1 prints red callout numerals 1, 2, 3, 4 down the first column, 33-36 down the ninth and 61-64 down the last, and the panel's own legend rows say the same - `(up)1 ... 2(down)` over the upper bank of column 1 and `(up)3 ... 4(down)` under its lower bank, `(up)5 ... 6(down)` over column 2. The guide's 30 W note corroborates it independently: "top four leftmost (1,5,9,13) and four rightmost (49,53,57,61) and bottom four leftmost (4,8,12,16)" is exactly a four-per-column numbering. So port n sits in column ceil(n/4), odd ports are the upper cage of their bank and even the lower.

the-optical-wall.note: FOUR GANGS OF FOUR COLUMNS PER BANK. Dark-opening runs scanned along the four cage rows and fitted to x = first + floor(i/4)*B + (i mod 4)*p give, on the two cleanest rows, first 30.171 / 30.227, B 96.209 / 96.213, p 23.227 / 23.226, rms 0.023 / 0.021 mm, worst residual 0.047. 30.20 / 96.21 / 23.23 are used; the gutter is B - 4p = 3.29 mm. std/osfp@1's 23.1 x 13.5 aperture is seated centred on each column, so adjacent cages in a gang stand 0.13 apart. ROWS. The column-wall profile averaged over all sixteen columns puts the upper bank's shell at y 16.3-45.9 and the lower's at 51.5-80.8. Inside the upper shell the two openings read 17.2-30.3 and 32.3-45.0 with a 2 mm perforated band between them, centres 23.75 and 38.65 - a 14.90 row pitch, the same 14.897 the AIS800-64O measured - and inside the lower 52.6-65.2 and 67.4-80.4, centres 58.9 and 73.9. The registry apertures are centred on each bank at 31.15 and 66.25 with the 14.90 row pitch, so the cages sit at y 16.95, 31.85, 52.05 and 66.95. EACH GANG IS ONE SHELL: a bright frame 93.9 wide round each four-column block, gasket fingers along its top and bottom and a perforated band between the rows. The inter-bank strip (45.9-51.5) is plain black panel with no hole in it. WHICH WAY THE CAGES FACE IS HELD, NOT SETTLED (#799). Each bank pair is drawn upper 0 / lower 180. Figure 1 reads otherwise: both openings of the upper bank have the card slot low (vents across the top of port 1), both of the lower bank have it high (vents across the bottom of port 4) - each bank a stacked 2x1 cage seating its two modules the same way up, the lower bank on the underside of the board (OSFP MSA rev 5.22 sections 7.1, 7.6). That is 0/0 over 180/180, which is not what #799 first proposed (0/0 throughout), so the turn is left as drawn, every pair is named in stack-exceptions, and the gap stacked-osfp-orientation says what settles it.

the-port-lamps-are-four-per-column.note: FOUR ROUND LENSES PER COLUMN IN THE LEGEND ROW, i.e. TWO PER PORT. Bright blobs on the legend baselines, binned by offset from their column centre across all sixteen columns, put lenses at -6.08 (n=33), -1.82 (n=43), +1.95 (n=40) and +6.00 (n=31), sd 0.26-0.33; they are seated symmetric at -6.0, -1.9, +1.9, +6.0 on centres y 14.85 above the upper bank and 82.55 below the lower (see the-legends for why not 15.10 / 82.75). The lens reads 1.2-1.6 across; common/led-dot@1 (2.0) is seated on the measured centres. OWNERSHIP IS NOT PUBLISHED. The left pair is given to the port whose `(up)` arrow and numeral are on the left (the upper cage) and the right pair to the lower, which is what the legend's layout suggests and nothing states. No document describes a port lamp at all - see the port-lamp-meaning gap.

the-rear.note: Read on Figure 2 at 5.512 x 5.540 px/mm. From the left: a 10.4 mm strip carrying two bosses, the PSU-3 and PSU-4 legends, an earth symbol and the grounding bracket; PSU-3 over PSU-4 at x 10.4-66.6 (read 10.1-66.9 including the frame lines; seated at the supply's 56.2 width, see celestica/psu-2000-ac@1); a 14.55 mm strip with five bosses and a black screw; FAN-3, FAN-2 and FAN-1 at x 81.25, 178.55 and 275.85 (97.3 pitch, 81.4 wide, the block centred on the chassis) with a 16 mm strip after each carrying its FAN-n legend and four bosses; a 14.55 mm strip with five bosses and a black screw; PSU-1 over PSU-2 at x 371.9-428.1; and a 10.4 mm strip with three bosses and the PSU-1 and PSU-2 legends. The two supply pairs are one face drawn four times, not mirrored. Bosses are drawn as the dark rings the figure shows; whether they are standoffs, PEM nuts or plugged holes is not stated.

the-sfp28-lamps.note: FOUR TRIANGLES, POINTING down-up-down-up from left to right, at x 405.07, 407.97, 411.57 and 414.47 on y 63.9 (the drawn offsets from the cage centre, -4.52/-1.80/+1.81/+4.83, are symmetrised to +/-1.8 and +/-4.7). The up-pointing pair is given to port 65 above and the down-pointing pair to 66 below, on the arrows' say-so; nothing documents them.

the-system-lamps-and-between-them.note: BETWEEN STAT/ALM, ALM/PSU AND PSU/FAN THE FIGURE DRAWS THREE SMALL LIGHT SQUARES that no callout names and no legend marks. They could be unlit lenses, light pipes or screw heads; at 5.5 px/mm they are four pixels across. They are not drawn and not punched - see the unlabelled-system-windows gap.

the-vent-fields.note: THE TOP FIELD: three rows of vertical slots about 1.1 x 2.0 across x 46.1-403.1 on a 2.973 mm pitch (121 slots, first to last), rows centred at about 4.9, 8.0 and 11.1 - drawn as the `slots` tile scaled to 2.9732 x 3.1. The field stops short of the CONSOLE legend. THE EDGE LATTICES: at each end of the face two columns of square windows about 2.7 wide on a 6.12 mm vertical pitch (bars measured at y 6.7, 12.95, 19.06 ... 80.2 on both columns), x 6.7-9.9 and 11.2-14.4 on the left and the mirror on the right. The figure shows the chassis interior through them, which is what makes them openings and not paint. OUTBOARD OF THEM, x 0-5.4 and 433.1-438.5, is a band of silver framing and further openings partly hidden behind the rack-mount latch; it is left as body metal.
